title: Technical debt identified in the docs before 2026-10-13
description:
Debt the project's documents (research.md open checks, decisions.md, README limitations) had already named, filed
so it is tracked in one place. Product features that are designed but not built (pauses, forks, scheduled world code,
durable messages) are direction, in plan.md, not debt.

## Operator decision

- "init br, file tasks I don't want them fixed now, existing identified technical debt should be fixed too create beads, i agree with your recommendations file those and the ones you chose not to show as beads, reformulate docs to reflect the future direction and remove old cruft, commit." (2026-10-13)

This approves: filing this debt as beads; none is approved for work until scheduled.

Filing is not scheduling: no bead here is to be worked until the operator schedules it ("I don't want them fixed now").
Nothing else is approved: test edits or removals, gate, guard or lint changes, refactoring beyond a bead's scope, and
every other policy question go back to the operator. A child inherits this section.

title: REST authentication: who may develop, who may call
description:
There is no authentication: anyone on the tailnet can call every route, the Claude account routes included
(README 'Interfaces'; decisions.md open decision 5). The question of who may call `develop` versus `call`, and how a
world's end user is told apart from its author, is open and the operator's to decide. Depends on the page-origin bead,
since same-origin world pages would defeat any cookie-based scheme.
acceptance_criteria: Operator decision recorded in decisions.md; then routes enforce it, with tests for each role.

title: Remove the one-time move of world data from cells to their runtime isolates
description:
`WorldCell.moveDataToRuntime` (src/cell/world-cell.ts:99) and `RuntimeFacet.importData` move rows from an older
build's cell table into the facet, guarded by a flag. Every world on the node moved on 2026-10-07; decisions.md says the
code can go once cells from older builds cannot appear. The old `world_data` tables are kept as backups.

Wanted: the operator confirms no older cell can appear; then the move code, its flag and `sqlDataRecords` go, and the
docs stop mentioning them. Whether to drop the backup tables is the operator's call.
acceptance_criteria: No reference to importData/moveDataToRuntime remains; tests and typecheck pass; deployed worlds keep their data.

title: Inject the page client with HTMLRewriter instead of a regular expression
description:
`appPage` finds `<head>` with a regular expression to inject the `world.call` client (src/cell/app-page.ts).
HTMLRewriter was spiked on celld (research.md): it handles any case and attributes on `<head>`, but a page without
`<head>` gets nothing, so a fallback is still needed. Likely to change with the page-origin bead; do that first.
acceptance_criteria: Pages with and without `<head>` get the client; under celld dev.

title: Snapshot rows larger than 1.44 MB
description:
A 1.44 MB snapshot row round-trips through a cell's SQLite on the node; larger is untested, and celld documents no
row or blob limit (research.md, open check 2). A raw snapshot passes 2 MB at about 410 definitions.

Wanted: the largest row the node stores measured; chunking only if a limit is found below realistic sizes.
acceptance_criteria: The measured limit recorded in research.md; a test of the chunked path if chunking is built.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: pw-djz.5 (snapshots as content-addressed pages) would remove the single large row: 4 KB pages, 65 KB stored per revision instead of 1408 KB.

title: Measure celld's remaining unknowns on the node
description:
Open in research.md: CPU limits per cell (open check 1); eviction timing and alarm retry limits, to tune the 30 s
heartbeat (open check 4); streaming lag from about 90 ms durable progress commits (open check 5); what wakes a cell after
a node restart; whether an idle world's isolate is released, and when.

Wanted: each measured on the node and recorded, with the setting it justifies (heartbeat, progress interval).
acceptance_criteria: Each item answered in research.md with what ran and what it showed, or marked not measurable with why.

title: Calls between worlds and run resumption across two nodes
description:
The fleet has one node. Untested: the latency of a `peerCall` forwarded to another node, what a caller sees when
the callee's node dies mid-call (celld retries a remote RPC only when the peer attempt did not start the method), and a
run resuming on another node after its owner dies (research.md open check 6, 'Not verified'; plan.md milestone 8).
acceptance_criteria: Results from a two-node fleet recorded in research.md.

title: `execute` previews still write for real in worlds they call
description:
`execute` rolls back its own world's data writes, but a world it reaches through `worlds.call` writes for real
(decisions.md open decision 3, README limitations). An agent's test run can therefore change another world's data.
What a preview should do there is the operator's decision.
acceptance_criteria: Operator decision recorded; the chosen behaviour tested.

title: Deep review: pi-world's performance limits and design, from raw evidence
description:
The 2026-10-13 performance and design review read the code and the project's own documents, and measured one defect
under vitest. This bead is the deeper version of that same review: same scope (pi-world's performance, concurrency and
parallelism limits, and its design decisions), but from raw evidence, against stated objectives, with checks that
could have failed. It produces findings and beads, not fixes.

## The task, as the operator's prompt

Find the performance, concurrency and parallelism limits of pi-world as deployed, and challenge its design, from
evidence rather than from the documents. Treat README.md, design.md and research.md as claims to verify, not facts.

1. Objectives first. Before looking for problems, propose the numbers the system must meet, for the operator to
   approve: p50 and p99 latency of a direct call, of a chain of three worlds and of a develop with N checks; the
   longest one world may stall another; worlds per node; sustained calls per second per world. Every later finding
   names the objective it violates.
2. Raw material. Start from the node's celld logs and metrics, the live worlds' snapshots, data and call patterns,
   and the source of celld, quickjs-wasi and pi-durable wherever their behaviour is undocumented.
3. A workload model and a load harness. Derive the workload from step 2. Commit a reproducible, open-loop load
   generator that is safe against coordinated omission and reports HdrHistogram percentiles. Record baselines.
4. Capacity per resource. For each resource (the shared cell isolates, each world's facet isolate, the VM pool, the
   cell's SQL queue, durable writes to the bucket, celld's per-cell request limit), predict its capacity with
   queueing arithmetic (Little's law, utilization), then measure utilization, saturation and errors (the USE method).
   A prediction that misses is itself a finding.
5. Profiles. Take V8 CPU profiles or flamegraphs of the cell and of a facet under the load, and name the hot paths
   with their share.
6. The concurrency protocol, model-checked. Specify develop, call, commit, the VM pool and the data overlay in TLA+.
   Check atomicity, no lost revision, and no call seeing an uncommitted heap with TLC. First show the checker red on
   a seeded bug.
7. Each challenged decision, demonstrated. For every design decision the review challenges, show the problem
   with a measurement or a working proof-of-concept under `celld dev`, not with an argument.

Deliver: findings ranked by objective violated, each with file:line, the measurement, profile, counterexample or
proof-of-concept that shows it, and a bead per finding. No fixes. Every number says what ran, where, and what it
showed; whatever did not run is marked not verified.

## What shows it is right (not the agent, not the operator)

- Measurements on the node, against objectives approved beforehand: numbers that could have failed.
- The committed load harness, which anyone can rerun to reproduce the baselines.
- TLC finding no counterexample in the model, after it was seen to find the seeded bug.
- A working proof-of-concept or measurement for each challenged decision.

## Objectives (approved 2026-10-14)

Measured from a client on the node over loopback (tailnet reported alongside, not judged); warm = facet isolate
resident and head blob in the cell; open-loop, at least 60 s and 10^4 samples per point, HdrHistogram p50/p99/p99.9
with error counts; a develop is timed from tool start to accepted, durable commit included, model call excluded.

| Id | Objective | Number |
|---|---|---|
| O1a | Direct call, read-only, warm, at the O6 rate | p50 <= 10 ms, p99 <= 50 ms |
| O1b | Direct call writing one key, warm, at the O6 rate | p50 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 250 ms |
| O1c | Cold call (first after eviction, head in R2) | p99 <= 1 s |
| O2 | Chain of three worlds A->B->C, read-only, warm, 10 calls/s | p50 <= 30 ms, p99 <= 100 ms |
| O3 | Develop with P plain and Q property checks (N = 0, 1, 10 of each) | p50 <= 150 + 10P + 300Q ms; p99 <= 2x that |
| O4 | Stall one world may cause another (victim: warm read-only call at 10/s) | victim p99 rises <= 50 ms over its baseline |
| O5a | Resident worlds per node (have run a call) | >= 300, to be pinned to the node's measured memory |
| O5b | Registered worlds per node, mostly evicted | >= 5 000, with O1c holding |
| O5c | Node aggregate: 100 resident worlds at 5 calls/s each | O1a holds |
| O6a | Sustained read-only calls per world | >= 100/s with O1a |
| O6b | Sustained writing calls per world | >= 50/s with O1b |
| O7 | Errors at or below the rated rate | 0 refusals, 0 failures |
| O8 | Overload at 2x rated | excess refused explicitly within 1 s; no queue wait > 1 s; accepted requests keep p99 |
| O9 | One operation is bounded | no call, develop or check holds a resource > 5 s |

## Operator decision

- "init br, file tasks I don't want them fixed now, existing identified technical debt should be fixed too create beads, i agree with your recommendations file those and the ones you chose not to show as beads, reformulate docs to reflect the future direction and remove old cruft, commit. Future work beads I want a deeper version of this task, not a bigger one. Before rewriting it: (1) say what a top professional in this field would do here that I'm not asking for; (2) name the rawest material they would start from instead of what has already been digested for me; (3) name the specific methods and tools they would use; (4) say what, other than you or me, would show the result is right. Then rewrite my prompt to ask for exactly that." (2026-10-13)
- "I approve of your suggestions and give you my permission to perform those tasks, optimize code, do the necessary refactorings and modifications." (2026-10-14, answering the proposed objectives and the access list: read-only access to the node's logs, metrics, snapshots and data; disposable `loadtest-*` worlds on the node; each load run against the node requested separately with its rate, duration and target; local `celld dev` work, profiles and TLA+ without further approval.)
- "I approve, good job so far I believe we can drive real improvement here way past original parameters" (2026-10-14, answering the request to run the ten listed scenarios against oracle-arm — read-call 100/s, write-call 50/s, chain 10+10/s, develop 0.5/s, stall, cold-call, overload 200/s, failure-storm 50+50/s, slow-overload, lost-update — from a node:25-slim container on the node over loopback, on disposable `loadtest-*` worlds, about 15 minutes in all, the `worlds` scenario excluded; and to deploy the fixed build with `npm run deploy` and rerun them.)
- "everything becomes loops, graphs, orchestration, and workflows" (2026-10-14: direction for the tooling.)

This approves: scheduling this review now; the listed load runs against oracle-arm, before and after a deploy; deploying fixed builds to the node with `npm run deploy`; the objectives above; read-only access to the node; disposable
`loadtest-*` worlds on the node; local proof-of-concepts, profiles and TLA+; fixes, optimizations and the refactorings
they need, for the findings this review makes. Not approved: any load run against the node beyond the runs listed above without its own approval
(rate, duration, target), the `worlds` scenario on the node, editing a test or gate to get a green (cm-shm), and any policy decision not listed here.
Every other policy question goes back to the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Approved objectives; committed load harness with baselines from the node; USE table per resource with predictions and measurements; profiles; a TLA+ model checked by TLC (seen red on a seeded bug); a measurement or proof-of-concept per challenged decision; a bead per finding.

title: Pooled call VMs return to the head without a new WebAssembly instance
description:
Every call rebuilt a WebAssembly instance: `VmPool.recycle` restored each VM through `QuickJS.restore`
(`git show a781c76:src/world/vm-pool.ts`, line 71). Profile `perf/profiles/read-call-2026-10-14T012818Z` (celld dev,
100 calls/s): restore 31.4 % of celld's CPU, instantiation 22.2 %. Objectives O1a, O6a, O8.

Done in `7106067`: `rewindInPlace` (`src/world/quickjs-rewind.ts`) copies the snapshot over the VM's own memory, with
a property test against a fresh restore (`test/quickjs-rewind.test.ts`, seeded bugs red). Measured: dev p99 31 → 12
ms and CPU 70 → 37 % of a core at 100/s; node p99 119 → 60 ms, CPU 42 → 23 % (`perf/results/node/read-call-*`).
acceptance_criteria: Property test green and red on seeded bugs; node read-call before and after recorded.
close_reason: Fixed in 7106067; property test red on seeded bugs; node read-call p99 119 -> 60 ms, CPU 42 -> 23 % (perf/results/node/read-call-*).

title: One snapshot cache per world's isolate, and no idle workbench VM
description:
In the runtime facet the workbench (`src/world/local-workbench.ts`) and the call runner
(`src/world/local-call-runner.ts`) each fetch and deserialize the head: after a develop the facet sends the heap to
the cell and the next call fetches it back over two RPC hops; after a wake the workbench restores a VM only to read
the catalogue. The workbench also keeps a whole VM for the life of the facet. Wanted: one cache of the head's snapshot
per isolate, filled by the heap a develop made, and a workbench that holds no VM between changes.
acceptance_criteria: A develop followed by a call makes no blob fetch (counted in a test); memory per resident world measured lower.

title: perf: split Context into a phase runner and a judge
description:
`perf/lib/scenario.ts` Context runs load phases, samples, judges verdicts and holds the operator client. Wanted:
verdict logic testable without a celld host, one responsibility per file (cm-f19).
acceptance_criteria: Verdict helpers unit-tested; scenarios unchanged in behaviour (same result files for the same run).

title: Model-check develop, call, commit, the VM pool and the overlay
description:
TLA+ in `spec/tla/`: atomicity of a call's writes, no lost revision, no call on an uncommitted heap, pool bounds and
liveness, and serializability of calls, each seen red on a seeded bug first, for the code as deployed (`a781c76`) and
as fixed. `npm run tla` reruns it.
acceptance_criteria: spec/tla/check.sh passes: every seeded bug red, every property of the fixed version green, the deployed lost update red with its trace.

title: Scenarios for O5b and O5c
description:
No scenario covers O5b (5 000 registered worlds, mostly evicted, with O1c holding) or O5c (100 resident worlds at
5 calls/s each, with O1a holding). Wanted: both in perf/, run under celld dev, and on the node only with the operator's
approval of the run.
acceptance_criteria: Both scenarios committed with dev results.

title: Explain the node's read-call p99 of 60 ms at 23 % CPU
description:
On oracle-arm at 100 read-only calls/s the p99 is 59.6 ms (O1a: 50) while celld uses 23 % of one core
(`perf/results/node/read-call-2026-10-14T022237Z.json`). celld is not CPU-bound; the node shares 2 vCPUs with about
twenty services. Wanted: the cause, from a profile or trace on the node itself (the profiling celld of pw-djz is
x86-64 only), and a finding with its fix or its bound.
acceptance_criteria: The p99 tail attributed with evidence from the node (profile, steal time or celld OTEL spans); O1a judged again.

title: Refuse a call within a second of its arrival, whatever the isolate is doing
description:
O8 asks that excess be refused within 1 s. Calls now carry a start deadline and are refused as busy when they reach
the runner late (`src/world/local-call-runner.ts`), but a single-threaded isolate sees a late call only after the
call before it ends: at twice capacity the longest wait is 1.17 s on dev and 1.34 s on the node, refusals at 1.2 s
(`perf/results/node/slow-overload-2026-10-14T023616Z.json`). Wanted: a call that cannot start within its second is
refused within it, for example by admission the cell predicts from the world's in-flight calls and completion rate;
calls that only await other worlds must not be refused by that prediction.
acceptance_criteria: slow-overload on the node: accepted wait and refusal p99 both ≤ 1 s; read-call and chain unchanged.

title: Writes on one node wait for the bucket
description:
A one-node fleet proves every write in the bucket; the node's log says so ("fleet durability requested and no
peer is available; writes wait for the bucket"). Writing calls: p50 164 to 170 ms, p99 303 ms (O1b: 120 / 250),
before and after every fix (`perf/results/node/write-call-*`). celld's docs give about 25 ms for a fleet proof
against about 600 ms for a bucket proof in their lab. A second node is the operator's decision (cost, network).

## Operator decision

None: whether to add a node, or to change O1b, goes back to the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Operator decision recorded; if a second node is added, write-call on the node meets O1b.

title: Store snapshots as content-addressed pages
description:
Every revision stores, hashes, replicates and later gzips the whole 1.4 MB linear memory as one blob
(`src/world/world.ts` accept, `src/revision/tiered-blob-store.ts`). A develop with no checks costs about 200 ms on the
node (O3: 150). Develop profile `perf/profiles/develop-2026-10-14T013843Z`: gzip about 33 %, blob replication 17 %,
SQLite 13 %, SHA-256 10 %. Over 22 revisions of the node's own sources, 4 KB content-addressed pages would store 65 KB
per revision instead of 1408 KB (`npm run bench:snapshot-pages`). Wanted: a revision stores only what it changed;
existing whole-blob revisions keep opening; snapshots stay byte-identical for determinism. Relates to pw-16t.4.
acceptance_criteria: develop on the node meets O3 at N = 0; existing worlds open unchanged; determinism tests pass.

title: Separate isolates do not isolate CPU on a 2-core node
description:
README says worlds do not slow each other. On oracle-arm (2 vCPUs) a call computing in one world raised another
world's p99 by 65 ms after the fixes, and 200 cheap calls/s into one world by 98 ms
(`perf/results/node/stall-2026-10-14T022952Z.json`); O4 allows 50. celld has no CPU quota per isolate. Wanted: a
stated bound on what one world's CPU costs others on a node of N cores, enforced or documented, and README corrected.
Relates to pw-uhd.6.
acceptance_criteria: stall on the node meets O4 for every phase, or the bound is the operator's and documented.

title: Store and archive snapshots outside the shared cell isolate
description:
After the workbench move (pw-rxw.3) a develop's remaining work in the shared cell isolate is storing its blob and
gzipping the previous one for R2 (`src/revision/tiered-blob-store.ts`, `src/cell/r2-archive.ts`): on celld dev a develop
with 3 property checks at 1/s still raised another world's p99 by 73 ms (O4: 50). Wanted: the per-revision byte work
happens in the world's own isolate or not at all (pw-djz.5 may remove it).
acceptance_criteria: stall on celld dev and the node: develop with property checks within O4.

title: Forgetting a world leaves it resident
description:
`DELETE /api/worlds/:id` removes the directory entry only (`src/worker.ts:32`); the world's cell, runtime facet and
loaded-worker slot stay until celld restarts, so forgotten worlds count against the 255-world limit (pw-djz.9) and
memory. What deleting a world should do with its storage (keep, archive, destroy) is the operator's decision.

## Operator decision

None: the semantics of deleting a world go back to the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Operator decision recorded; a deleted world gives back its loaded-worker slot (worlds scenario under celld dev).

title: A node holds at most 255 worlds per deploy
description:
Each world's runtime is a Dynamic Worker with a loader id of its own (`src/isolate/host/runtime-loader.ts:14`).
celld allows 255 per script and generation (`crates/celld/js.rs:7252-7255`, v0.6.1) and frees one only when its handle
is collected. The node never evicts an idle cell (`CELLD_IDLE_EVICT_S` unset). Under celld dev the 255th world failed
at creation: `too many loaded workers for script "pi-world" in generation 1 (limit 255)`
(`perf/results/dev/worlds-2026-10-14T011908Z.json`). With `CELLD_IDLE_EVICT_S=5`, 320 of 320 opened and answered, at
2.1 GB instead of 4.36 GB at 255; a cold call after eviction took at most 491 ms on the node (O1c holds). O5a.
Options: set idle eviction on the node (an infrastructure change, trading warm calls for capacity), several worlds
per loaded worker (trading isolation), or both.

## Operator decision

None: the node's eviction setting and the isolation trade-off go back to the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Operator decision recorded; the worlds scenario reaches O5a on the node's configuration.

title: Design direction from the 2026-10-13 review
description:
The design review of 2026-10-13 challenged nine decisions; the operator agreed with every recommendation. Each
child states one, with the evidence found. Together they are the direction the docs now describe (plan.md).

## Operator decision

- "init br, file tasks I don't want them fixed now, existing identified technical debt should be fixed too create beads, i agree with your recommendations file those and the ones you chose not to show as beads, reformulate docs to reflect the future direction and remove old cruft, commit." (2026-10-13)

This approves: the nine recommendations as the project's direction, with the policy choices they carry: world pages served from an origin of their own; calls made serializable (conflicts detected, the call rerun); develops, checks, enrolment, rollback and prelude upgrades moved into the world's own isolate; a time budget with a stable meaning that bounds a whole operation; incidents grouped by kind with bounded durable writes; `data.list` that never truncates silently; the domain free of pi-durable, with `World` split by responsibility; newly created worlds may call no other world until granted; source-log replay as the upgrade path for a new QuickJS build. The exact numbers inside them (budgets, caps, origins) are not approved and go back to the operator.

Filing is not scheduling: no bead here is to be worked until the operator schedules it ("I don't want them fixed now").
Nothing else is approved: test edits or removals, gate, guard or lint changes, refactoring beyond a bead's scope, and
every other policy question go back to the operator. A child inherits this section.

title: World pages are served from an origin of their own
description:
`/w/:id/` (src/worker.ts:37, src/cell/app-page.ts) serves HTML that the agent wrote, on the same origin as
`/api/*` and the operator UI. Script on such a page can call `develop`, `rollback`, `DELETE /api/worlds/:id`, the
`/api/account/*` routes (log out, replace the Claude token) and every other world's routes. Adding cookie-based
authentication later would not help: the page's script carries the cookies. Today the tailnet is the only perimeter.

Wanted: a world's page cannot reach the operator API or another world's page with the operator's authority. It may
still call its own world's functions (the injected `world.call`). Choosing the mechanism (a subdomain per world, a
separate host, a sandboxed frame with a strict CSP) needs the operator's answer on the domain and TLS set-up of the
node.
acceptance_criteria: A proof-of-concept page that calls `POST /api/worlds/:id/develop` from a world page succeeds before the change and fails after it, run under `celld dev`; `world.call` from the page still works; README/design.md describe the boundary.

title: Calls are serializable: a call that read data another call changed is rerun
description:
Calls are atomic (writes buffered in `OverlayDataPort`, committed on success) but not isolated: of two calls that
read and write one key, the one finishing last wins (design.md, "Calls run concurrently"). A call that reads a counter,
awaits another world, then writes it, loses an increment made by a call that committed meanwhile. Calls discard their
heap and buffer their writes, so a call can be rerun safely: the overlay could record what it read and the commit check
it.

Wanted: concurrent calls behave as if run one at a time (serializable); a conflict is detected at commit and the
call rerun at the head it started from, a bounded number of times, after which it fails as a conflict (an incident).
`execute` keeps its preview semantics. Data writes reached through another world (`worlds.call`) are outside the
transaction and stay so; document it.
acceptance_criteria: A test with two calls interleaved across a peer await that increments one key ends at +2 (red today at +1); a stateful property test (Hegel) over random interleavings finds no lost update; design.md describes the guarantee and the retry bound.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: Implemented in 7106067, a9acdf5, 3e34ae7: reads recorded and validated at commit, stale calls rerun in a per-world lane, at most 5 reruns then failure 'conflict' (an incident). Test: 8 concurrent read-await-write increments end at +8 (red before). Node: 20 concurrent increments left a count of 3 before (perf/results/node/lost-update-2026-10-14T020057Z.json). Outstanding: the Hegel stateful property test over random interleavings, and design.md. Reruns repeat calls to other worlds; documented in design.md.

title: Develops, checks, enrolment, rollback and prelude upgrades run in the world's own isolate
description:
Calls run in each world's own isolate (a facet loaded through a Worker Loader), but every change still runs on
`World`'s main VM inside the world's cell, which shares a small pool of isolates (`worker_count=2`) with every other
world's cell (research.md, open check 10). Any CPU a develop spends holds up unrelated worlds: a develop evaluates its
source, every check, a property check on up to 50 inputs, each with a whole budget. The 2026-10-13 fix bounded the
worst case (a hang no longer shrinks), but a check that finishes just inside its budget still costs 50 budgets, in the
shared isolate. It also leaves two VM runtimes per world and snapshots crossing isolates in both directions.

Wanted: all VM work of a world (calls, previews, attempts, enrolment, rollback, prelude upgrade, opening the head's
catalogue) happens in that world's isolate; the cell keeps durability, the revision/rejection/check documents, the
lock and the agent. The core stays testable in process behind a port, as `CallRunner` is today.
acceptance_criteria: On celld dev: a develop whose check computes for several seconds leaves another world's call answering in under 100 ms (measured before: held for the whole develop); all existing tests pass against the in-process adapter; design.md, README architecture and research open check 10 updated.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: Implemented in 822db16 (Workbench port; the facet does all VM work of changes). celld dev: a develop computing 2.4 s at 1/s raised another world's p99 by 35 ms (was 2028 ms); node +23 ms (was +464), perf/results/node/stall-*. All tests pass on the in-process adapter. Outstanding: design.md, README architecture, research open check 10. The blob store and archive still run in the cell isolate: pw-djz.7.

title: The time budget has a stable meaning and bounds a whole operation
description:
`VmLimits.budget` counts QuickJS interrupt ticks (30 000 by default, world-vm.ts:47). A tick is about 0.1 ms in
Node but far slower and code-dependent in a runtime isolate: a loop calling `Date.now()` ran 70 s before the budget
stopped it, a plain loop 30 million iterations in 7 s (research.md, open check 11). Each evaluation gets a whole
budget, so a develop costs up to (1 + checks x (50 + counterexample + 50)) budgets. In Workers, `Date.now()` does not
advance during synchronous execution, which is why ticks were used.

Wanted: the operator can state a budget in time for a call and for a whole develop (source and every check
together), and the limit holds within a stated tolerance on the node. The numbers are the operator's to set.
acceptance_criteria: Measured on the node: a loop of each kind (plain, Date.now-calling, allocation-heavy) stops within the stated tolerance of the stated time; a develop with many slow checks is rejected at the develop budget, naming it.

title: Incidents are grouped by kind and their durable writes are bounded
description:
An incident's key is the definition name plus the first line of the error (src/incident/incident.ts:47). An error
like `"no item " + id` opens a new incident, one durable commit (about 90 ms on the node), per distinct id. Every open
incident is listed in one `WorldIncidents` document (src/revision/documents.ts:63) rewritten by each record, so each
record costs more as incidents accumulate. `POST /call` is unauthenticated, so anyone on the tailnet can drive this,
and the commits share the cell's SQL queue with the agent's progress commits.

Wanted: one failing definition with a varying message is one incident; recording failures under load costs a bounded
number of durable writes per second per world; the open index does not grow one document without bound. The
grouping rule and the bounds are the operator's to set.
acceptance_criteria: A test where a definition throws with 1000 distinct ids yields one open incident; a load test of failing calls shows durable writes per second at or under the bound; design.md 'A failed call is an incident' updated.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: Bound done in 97c1b1f/4d25c8d: repeats of an open incident count in memory, shown to readers merged, written together at most every 30 s or before a retry or close. Node: good calls beside 50 failing calls/s p50 127 -> 3.2 ms, p99 460 -> 43 ms (perf/results/node/failure-storm-*). Outstanding, the operator's: the grouping rule (name + failure kind instead of name + first line of error); it changes test/incidents.test.ts cases that expect a new incident per message, and needs that approval (cm-shm).

title: `data.list` never truncates silently
description:
`data.list(prefix)` returns at most 1000 rows (`LIST_LIMIT`, src/isolate/runtime/sql-data-port.ts:4) with no sign
that rows were cut off, and the prelude does not document the limit. World code that sums or exports a list is wrong
once a world holds more than 1000 rows under a prefix. The REST `GET /data` has the same limit.

Wanted: world code and REST callers either see every row (through pages or a cursor) or get an explicit signal or
error; the prelude and README document it.
acceptance_criteria: A test with 1001 rows under one prefix sees all of them or an explicit truncation signal (red today); the prelude's doc text and README's data section describe the behaviour.

title: The world domain is free of pi-durable, and `World` is split by responsibility
description:
`World` (src/world/world.ts, 442 lines), `IncidentLog` and `NumberedLog` import pi-durable's `Session`, `Tx` and
document tokens and chord's `BACKGROUND_CONTEXT`, so the domain depends on the framework (against the project's
hexagonal rule: dependencies point inward). `World` also holds six responsibilities in one file: the head and
revisions, rejections, checks, grants, incidents, and routing calls.

Wanted: the domain reaches storage through a port of its own; pi-durable is an adapter; each responsibility lives in
its own file. Behaviour is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: No file under src/world, src/revision (domain part), src/incident or src/check imports @earendil-works/*, enforced by a check that fails the build (seen red first); the test suite passes unchanged; README's directory table updated.

title: A new world may call no other world until its owner grants it
description:
Grants default to "any" (`ANY_WORLD`, src/world/world.ts:99, src/world/grants.ts), for every world, new ones
included. The code calling other worlds is written by the agent. The operator's 2026-10-12 default ("existing worlds
may call any world until the operator restricts them") stays for existing worlds; the 2026-10-13 decision makes newly
created worlds start with no grants.
acceptance_criteria: A world created after the change lists no other worlds and is refused a call until granted; a world created before keeps 'any'; guide.md and README's grants text say so.

title: Source-log replay rebuilds a world, as the upgrade path for a new QuickJS build
description:
Snapshots load only with the exact `quickjs.wasm` build that wrote them (quickjs-wasi pinned at 3.6.2). The
documented upgrade path, replaying accepted `develop` sources into a fresh VM (plan.md milestone 7), is not built, so
upgrading QuickJS would strand every world. Develops are deterministic (pinned clock, seeded random, no host calls),
so replay is possible today.

Wanted: a world can be rebuilt from its revisions' sources (rollbacks and prelude upgrades included) into a VM that
gives the same catalogue and passes its checks; the operator can run it per world; the docs describe it as the upgrade
path. Whether the log becomes authoritative (open decision 4) stays open.
acceptance_criteria: A test replays a world with develops, a rollback and a prelude upgrade and gets an identical catalogue, and byte-identical snapshots on the same build; replay of every world on the node verified before a QuickJS upgrade.

title: Performance and concurrency findings left open on 2026-10-13
description:
The 2026-10-13 performance pass fixed two defects (a hung property check shrinking 200 times; the VM pool keeping
more VMs warm than asked) and chose not to fix these. Each needs a measurement on the node or the operator's
scheduling first.

## Operator decision

- "init br, file tasks I don't want them fixed now, existing identified technical debt should be fixed too create beads, i agree with your recommendations file those and the ones you chose not to show as beads, reformulate docs to reflect the future direction and remove old cruft, commit." (2026-10-13)

This approves: filing these findings as beads; none is approved for work until scheduled.

Filing is not scheduling: no bead here is to be worked until the operator schedules it ("I don't want them fixed now").
Nothing else is approved: test edits or removals, gate, guard or lint changes, refactoring beyond a bead's scope, and
every other policy question go back to the operator. A child inherits this section.

title: Measure whether snapshot reads wait behind agent commits in the cell's SQL queue
description:
Every SQL operation of a world cell goes through one queue (`cellDatabase`, src/cell/sqlite-database.ts), as
pi-durable's facade requires. The runtime facet fetches a new head's snapshot through `WorldCell.blobBytes`, which
reads through that queue, behind pi-durable's progress commits (about 90 ms each on the node, spaced 400 ms). So the
first call after a new revision, while the agent is streaming, may wait. Not measured: it shows only on the node.

Wanted: a measurement of the first-call latency after a develop, with and without a streaming agent run; if it is
material, the head's snapshot reaches the facet without waiting on the queue.
acceptance_criteria: Numbers from the node for both cases, recorded in research.md; a fix only if the difference is material.

title: A counterexample re-run starts from the developed heap, as enrolment does
description:
In `firstBrokenCheck` (src/world/attempt.ts:55-60) the counterexample is applied to the heap as the check's
verdict run left it; there is no reset to the developed heap between them, while `attemptEnrolment` resets between the
same two steps (attempt.ts:91) and the doc comment says each check starts from the developed heap. A check whose
expression changes heap state (a call that bumps state) can therefore be seen failing, or not, differently at a
develop than at its enrolment.
acceptance_criteria: A test with a state-bumping check whose counterexample's effect depends on that state is red today and green after; the doc comment matches the code.

title: VmPool: cover the reset-failure path and drop fixed sleeps from its tests
description:
Stryker on src/world/vm-pool.ts (2026-10-13) leaves the path where `vm.reset` throws during recycling with no
coverage (vm-pool.ts, `recycle`'s catch). test/vm-pool.test.ts waits a fixed 50 ms for background recycling 17 times,
which costs about 0.85 s per run and can race on a slow machine.

Wanted: the reset-failure path is tested (the VM is disposed, the slot freed); the tests wait for recycling to finish
deterministically rather than by a timer.
acceptance_criteria: Stryker shows no uncovered mutant in vm-pool.ts; the test file has no fixed sleeps.

title: Kill the surviving mutants of the shrinker
description:
Stryker on src/check/shrink.ts (2026-10-13): 86.5 %, 14 survivors in code older than that day, e.g. the
deletion-window bounds, `lowerChoices`' filter and `smaller`'s comparisons. Some may be equivalent mutants.

Wanted: each survivor is either killed by a test or recorded as equivalent with the reason.
acceptance_criteria: A Stryker run on shrink.ts with every survivor killed or listed as equivalent in the bead's close reason.

title: Calls between worlds under celld's per-cell request limit
description:
celld refuses a request with `503 cell request limit reached` when a cell has 64 in flight
(`CELLD_MAX_CELL_REQUESTS`), and the count includes the cell's own calls to other worlds: 40 concurrent calls that each
call another world got 28 answers and 12 refusals (research.md, open check 9). A world also waits without a deadline
for a free VM once its 8 are busy (`VmPool.slot`), so a burst queues in memory with no bound.

Wanted: a measured picture of where load is refused or queued along a chain of worlds, and a behaviour the operator
chooses (node setting, back-pressure, a bounded queue with a clear refusal).
acceptance_criteria: A load run on the node that records answers, refusals and queue waits per hop; the chosen behaviour documented in README 'Limits on one node'.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: Since 97c1b1f a call that cannot start within a second of arriving is refused as busy (503, Retry-After) before celld's 64-request limit is reached in the slow-overload scenario (dev: 230 busy refusals, no 'cell request limit reached'). Calls between worlds under the limit were not re-measured.

title: Decide whether calls that compute need more than one isolate per world
description:
A world's calls share one single-threaded isolate: calls overlap only while they await another world, and a call
that computes holds every other call of that world until it returns (research.md, "Memory per world"). The world's data
is synchronous SQLite inside that facet, which is what world code calls, so a second isolate cannot simply share it.

Wanted: a measurement of how often a world's calls queue behind a computing call on the node's real worlds, and a
recommendation (accept, or a design for parallel calls) for the operator.
acceptance_criteria: The measurement and recommendation recorded in research.md.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: Evidence from pw-djz: on the 2-core node a call computing in one world raised another's p99 by 65 ms and a flood of 200 cheap calls/s by 98 ms after the fixes (perf/results/node/stall-2026-10-14T022952Z.json); see pw-djz.6.
